catalog_quote: Wanga has two surface tones, High (H) and Low (L), but presents evidence for a three-way underlying tonal contrast: /H/, /L/, and /Ø/ (toneless). Tones associate with the mora as tone bearing unit (TBU). Evidence for the mora is clearest from tone spreading processes like Melodic Doubling where a Melodic H tone spreads rightward by one mora. ... Most phonetic L tones arise on /Ø/ TBUs, with L inserted by default. However, underlying /L/ is found with some noun tone melodies, the reflexive object marker, and one tonal class of verb roots (historically *H roots synchronically have initial /L/). Ls block H tone assignment (6) and anticipatory tone spreading (7). Toneless TBUs are transparent to these processes. ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Wanga is described purely as a tone language: surface H vs L, underlying three-way /H/ vs /L/ vs toneless, mora as TBU, lexical tone classes in nouns (8+ surface patterns) and verb roots (two classes) plus melodic (grammatical) H tones. The sketch's phonology section (vowels with length contrast neutralized word-initially/finally, open syllables, tone) contains no statement about word stress, accent or prominence, and no mention of penultimate lengthening. Corroborated first-hand by Akidah 2000 p.8 ('Luwanga like all its sister dialects of Luhya.. is tonal'; suprasegmentals excluded) and Ebarb, Green & Marlo 2014 p.135 ('Wanga is a central Luyia variety with a reversive tonal system').
new_statements.exceptions: none (no stress statement to qualify); vowel length contrast is neutralized to short word-initially and word-finally (sec. 2.1)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described for words in isolation and in phrasal contexts (HTA, HTI, phrase-medial H deletion); sentence-level tone explicitly still under study (fn. to sec. 4). No word-stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Wanga proper (Luwanga/Oluwanga, iso lwg = wang1294), spoken around Mumias/Matungu, Kakamega County. Green et al.'s data come mainly from consultant Alfred Anangwe and fieldwork 2006-2018; Green & Farris-Trimble's speaker is from Musamba; Mukanda's speakers from Matungu; Akidah's from Mumias. No dialect mismatch.
